steps.prompt: An ant on the outside of a box wants to walk to the opposite corner. A fly can fly straight through the air. Who has the shorter trip, and how could you work out the ant's?

cards.title: Space diagonals
cards.body: A box with edges $a$, $b$, $c$ has a space diagonal (through the inside, corner to opposite corner) of $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}$. A cube with edge $s$ has face diagonal $s\sqrt{2}$ and space diagonal $s\sqrt{3}$.

cards.title: Worked example: a box
cards.problem: A box is $2$ by $3$ by $6$. How long is its space diagonal?

try.prompt: How long is the space diagonal?

cards.title: Nets and counting
cards.body: To find the shortest path along the surface, unfold the faces flat (a net) and draw a straight line. Count faces $F$, edges $E$ and vertices $V$ with Euler's formula $V - E + F = 2$. A prism on an $n$-gon has $2n$ vertices, $3n$ edges and $n + 2$ faces.

cards.title: Worked example: the ant
cards.problem: An ant walks on the outside of a cube with edge $2$ from one corner to the opposite corner. How far must it walk?

steps.text: Unfold two faces into a $4 \times 2$ rectangle.

try.prompt: How long is the long side of the rectangle?
How far does it walk? Write it in simplest radical form, like 3√2.

cards.title: The common trap: through or along
cards.body: The space diagonal goes through the inside; a walk along the surface is longer. When unfolding, try each way and keep the shortest: put the two shorter edges together. A face diagonal is $s\sqrt{2}$, not $s\sqrt{3}$.

prompts: How do you decide which way to unfold a box?
